concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and elevated troponin T level, which are all indicative of acute myocardial infarction.
The patient's blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg, and the presence of thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery and elevated troponin T level suggest cardiogenic shock.
The patient presented with chest pain, ST-segment elevation, and ST-segment depression, which are all indicative of unstable angina.

concepts.preferred_label: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response
concepts.why: The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and the presence of normal sinus rhythm at presentation does not rule out the possibility of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.
The patient's history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and the presence of R/S greater than 1 in leads V1-V2 suggest the possibility of ventricular arrhythmia.
The patient has a history of diabetes, and the presence of elevated troponin T level and thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery suggest diabetic cardiomyopathy.
The patient's blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg, and the presence of contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion suggest hypotensive cardiac arrest.
The patient presented with pericardial effusion and thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, which are indicative of post-myocardial infarction pericarditis.
It explains the subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which is consistent with inferior wall myocardial infarction.

rationales.F01: Sudden-onset chest pain is a classic symptom of acute myocardial infarction.
rationales.F05: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF is indicative of inferior wall myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels are a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery is a common cause of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F12: Hypotension is a sign of cardiogenic shock, which can occur in the setting of myocardial infarction.
